_disclaimer: Illustrative card-voice example for a PRIVATE company. Numbers anchored to Stripe's 2024 annual letter (payment volume $1.4T), 2024-09 secondary tender at $91.5B, and analyst estimates for revenue/take rate/mix. P&L-style figures are analyst reconstructions, not issuer-disclosed.
_purpose: Hidden analyst fields the writer must resolve BEFORE composing card_slots.json prose. Updated for 4-card v2 layout.

intro_sentence.data_anchor: Stripe 2024 payment volume $1.4T +38% YoY vs PayPal $1.6T +9% / Adyen $1.3T +33%; private valuation $91.5B = GMV multiple 6.5% vs Adyen public 15%.
intro_sentence.variant_view: Consensus: private discount is permanent until IPO clarifies. Refined view: ~70% of the discount is liquidity premium that compresses post-IPO; the other 30% is Shopify-concentration risk that remains structural.
intro_sentence.falsifier: If 2025 Q4 Shopify Payments share of Stripe processing volume crosses 25% (vs current ~18%), the concentration risk re-rates and the IPO discount widens, not narrows.

primary_quote.speaker: Co-founder Patrick Collison
primary_quote.quote: Our next three years of growth will come from Connect and Issuing, not core payments — we have already built the payments rail; now we're building the platform on top.

company_focus_paragraph.data_anchor: Revenue mix evolution: FY2020 ~90% from core payments; FY2024 estimate ~30% from Connect platform fees + Issuing + Tax + Atlas. Gross margin trajectory ~65% (2020) → ~78% (2024) per public funding-round commentary.
company_focus_paragraph.variant_view: Bulls: Stripe is the developer-economy stack. Refined view: it's actually three businesses — payments processing (mature, take-rate capped), Connect (growth, ROE highest), and Issuing/Tax/Atlas (emerging, SaaS-style). Each has different valuation framework.

catalyst_with_date.event: Stripe IPO window — management has hinted at 2026-2027 readiness
catalyst_with_date.implication: IPO will force public valuation print; expect re-rate either to Adyen (~$130B) or to legacy payments multiple (~$70B).

industry_paragraph.data_anchor: Global digital payments TAM ~$200T+ processing volume; take rates compressed from 2.5% (2010) to 1.2-1.6% (2024) due to Visa/Mastercard rule changes + Reg II + scale. ACH/RTP replacing cards in B2B: from <5% (2020) to ~12% (2024) of US C2B+B2B flows.
industry_paragraph.variant_view: Consensus: payments is a mature commodity. Refined view: payments is mature, but adjacencies (embedded finance, AI-driven merchant tooling) are not — Stripe's 78% gross margin already reflects this shift, while pure-payments peers (PayPal 39%, Block 32%) don't.
industry_paragraph.falsifier: If Stripe gross margin compresses below 73% in any reported year, it would signal the adjacencies bet isn't working and the multiple should re-rate to PayPal/Block range.

primary_quote.speaker: Co-founder John Collison
primary_quote.quote: Payments is not a business — it's a feature of every internet business. Our job is to build what comes after payments.

five_year_arc.narrative.data_anchor: Valuation trajectory: 2021 $95B → 2023 $50B (recap at low) → 2024-02 $65B (tender) → 2024-09 $91.5B (secondary). Processing volume: 2020 $400B → 2024 $1.4T (~3.5x in 4 years). Revenue mix: payments-only → 5 product lines.
five_year_arc.narrative.variant_view: Consensus reads the 5-year arc as 'payments company with a venture-cycle drawdown.' Refined view: it's a 5-year SaaS-ification — same processing rail, but increasingly bundled with subscription-style products. Adyen never made this transition; PayPal failed to.
five_year_arc.narrative.falsifier: If FY2025 disclosed (post-IPO or via annual letter) SaaS/subscription revenue share is below 30%, the 'SaaS-ification' framing collapses and the multiple should compress to pure-payments comparables.

catalyst_with_date.event: Stripe IPO S-1 filing — first public segment disclosure
catalyst_with_date.implication: Will reveal actual mix of payments vs platform vs adjacencies revenue.

revenue_explainer_points.data_anchor: Processing volume comparison: Stripe $1.4T (+38%) vs PayPal $1.6T (+9%) vs Adyen $1.3T (+33%) vs Block $228B (+12%). Take rate ladder: PayPal 1.9% / Stripe 1.2% / Adyen 0.18%. Gross margin: Stripe 78% / Adyen 53% / PayPal 39%.
revenue_explainer_points.variant_view: Consensus: Stripe is mid-take-rate, mid-margin. Refined view: blended take rate hides the fact that Connect customers pay 1.5%+ while pass-through enterprise customers pay <0.5% — actual customer segmentation is barbell, not bell-curve.
revenue_explainer_points.falsifier: If Stripe annual letter shows blended take rate flat or declining 2024 → 2025, it signals enterprise mix shift is dominating and the platform-pricing thesis weakens.

primary_quote.speaker: Co-founder Patrick Collison
primary_quote.quote: Average take rate masks two very different businesses — the platform side, where developers pay for full-stack tooling, and the enterprise side, where we are essentially a payments utility.

cfa_lens.company_calculation.data_anchor: Residual income model: book equity B ~$8B; ROE estimate 30% (gross margin 78% × asset turnover); WACC k = 12% (private + growth-stage premium); excess return spread = 18pp → annual residual income $1.44B; 10-year PV of residual income ≈ $75B; total RI fair value $83B vs current $91.5B (premium ~10%).
cfa_lens.company_calculation.variant_view: Standard DCF gives ~$85B fair value; RI decomposition gives $78-88B; current $91.5B sits at top of RI range. The 5-15% premium represents 'IPO liquidity option' + 'AI merchant tooling option' that DCF underweights.
cfa_lens.company_calculation.falsifier: If FY2025 Stripe ROE compresses below 22% (vs current ~30%) AND IPO is delayed past 2027, the optionality premium collapses by ~$15-20B (RI fair value drops to $65-75B).
